chunks: Saad said: When Muhammad ibn Nasir was afflicted by the illness in which he died,

he was asked, while his tongue was heavy: 'To whom belongs this matter after you?' He said with a weak, stuttering tongue: 'Ahmad.' They did not know who he was, so after him they divided into three groups; one group said that it was his son, Ahmad. Another group said it was Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Furat. Another group said it was Ahmad ibn Abi al-Husayn ibn Bushr ibn Yazid. They scattered and did not return to anything.

key_terms.الْأَمْرُ: the matter/authority (referring to leadership or deputyship)

ai.seo_question: Who were the three groups that claimed succession after Muhammad ibn Nasir?
ai.summary: This hadith from Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* illustrates the critical period of *al-ghurba* (estrangement) following the death of Muhammad ibn Nasir, where the ambiguity of the name 'Ahmad' led to fragmentation among the followers. It highlights the scholarly concern with distinguishing the true Imam from false claimants during the Minor and Major Ghaiba, a theme central to Twelver Shia historiography. The disintegration into three factions underscores the necessity of clear designation (*nass*) to preserve communal unity and doctrinal integrity.
